deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page studies the series f(x)=Σ x^{2n}/(n!)^2. In modern terms f(x)=I_0(2x), the modified Bessel function. Gauss finds its large-x behaviour in logarithmic (exponent) form, its integral representation, its oscillating companion J_0(2x), and the product of the two.

(1) Top lines. The odd series x + x^3/2 + x^5/12 + x^7/144 + … equals Σ x^{2n+1}/(n!(n+1)!) = I_1(2x). The first attempt '1+xx+x^4/4+x^6/36+etc.' is struck out. Gauss writes
I_1(2x) ≈ A·√(1/x)·e^{2x − 3/(16x) − 3/(64x^2) − 21/(1024x^3) − 27/(2048x^4) − 1899/(163840x^5) − …}.
The whole correction series stands in the exponent: the comma/dot after e^{2x} continues the exponent, and the next page writes fx = A√(1/x)·e^{φx}. An earlier factor √2 (or 2/x) under the root is struck out. This is the asymptotic expansion of log I_1(2x).

(2) 'Pars const e^{2x cos φ} … = f x'. The constant Fourier term (mean over φ) of e^{2x cos φ} is I_0(2x) = f(x). The struck parenthesis was an abandoned attempt.

(3) The constant A = 0.2820948 = 1/(2√π). This is the leading factor, since I_0(z) ~ e^z/√(2πz) and at z = 2x this gives e^{2x}/(2√π·√x). A struck line gives ln(1/A) = 1.2654 ≈ π·0.40284. Then log10 A = 9.4503951 − 10.

(4) The main result:
f(x) = 1 + x^2 + x^4/4 + x^6/36 + x^8/576 + … ≈ A·x^{−1/2}·exp(2x + 1/(16x) + 1/(64x^2) + 25/(3072x^3) + 13/(2048x^4) + 1073/(163840x^5) + 103/(12288x^6)).
In the variable z = 2x this reads log I_0(z) = z − ½ log(2πz) + 1/(8z) + 1/(16z^2) + 25/(384z^3) + 13/(128z^4) + 1073/(5120z^5) + 103/(192z^6) + …

My derivation (confirming the coefficients): put u = I'/I. This satisfies the Riccati equation u' + u^2 + u/z − 1 − ν^2/z^2 = 0. Then expand u = 1 − 1/(2z) + Σ e_k z^{−k}. Equivalently, take the logarithm of the Hankel/Poisson series 1 + Σ ((2k−1)!!)^2/(k!·8^k·z^k).

(5) The alternating series 1 − x^2 + x^4/4 − x^6/36 + x^8/576 − … is J_0(2x). Gauss correctly states it is the constant term of cos(2x sin φ).

(6) 'Bisher durch Induction' ('so far by induction', i.e. found empirically, not proved). He gives the product
P = J_0(2x)·I_0(2x) = 1 − x^4/2 + x^8/96 − x^12/25920 + …
He rewrites the coefficients as
(−1)^n·[1/(1^2·2^2···(2n)^2)]·[2·6·10···(4n−2)/n!] = (−1)^n/((n!)^2·(2n)!).
So P = Σ (−1)^n x^{4n}/((n!)^2 (2n)!) = 0F3(;1/2,1,1;−x^4/4).
The next page continues with Q = (J_0^2 + I_0^2)/2. It also gives numerical values f(5), f(5i), f(4), f(4i) and a three-term recurrence for the Fourier coefficients of cos(2x cos φ).
errors: No mathematical errors found. The Hankel-type expansions behind (1) and (4) are only asymptotic (divergent), which Gauss does not remark on.
Struck line: ln(1/A) = ln(2√π) = 1.265512…, Gauss wrote 1.2654. This is a small slip in the last digit, and the line is cancelled anyway.
The product formula for P is explicitly marked as found by induction, not proved.

results.what: f(x)=Σx^{2n}/(n!)^2 = I_0(2x) is the constant Fourier term (mean) of e^{2x cos φ}; J_0(2x) is the constant term of cos(2x sin φ)
results.modern_name: Bessel/Poisson integral representations of I_0 and J_0
leading term of the asymptotic expansion of I_0 (Laplace's method)
asymptotic expansion of log I_0 (logarithmic form of the Hankel expansion; Debye/Riccati-type)
results.usually_credited_to: Expansion of I_ν/J_ν: Poisson 1823, Jacobi, Kummer 1837, Stokes 1850, Hankel 1869; logarithmic form is a standard reformulation

results.what: J_0(2x)·I_0(2x) = Σ (−1)^n x^{4n}/((n!)^2 (2n)!), found by induction
results.usually_credited_to: Products of Bessel series: Schläfli/Nielsen, late 19th century (Watson §5.41)

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's interest in the series Σx^{2n}/(n!)^2 and Bessel-type integrals is partly known from his Nachlass. Correct six-term asymptotic expansions of log I_0 and log I_1, plus an empirically found closed form for J_0·I_0, are a notable unpublished detail. They likely predate the systematic expansions of Hankel and the product formulas in Nielsen/Watson. However, the methods are routine for Gauss and the page is undated, so this is not a major new attribution.

transcription_corrections: The correction series after e^{2x} (both formulas) lies in the exponent: read A·√(1/x)·e^{2x − 3/16·x^{-1} − …} and A·√(1/x)·e^{2x + 1/16·x^{-1} + …}. The comma/dot after 2x is not a multiplication; cf. 'fx = A√(1/x)·e^{φx}' on the next page.
First formula prefactor: the image shows √ with a struck '2' (and a struck x below). The intended final form is A·√(1/x), not '√2·x'.
'Pars const e^{2x cos φ} … = A' should read '= f x' (the symbol after '=' is the same f-glyph as in the later 'f x'), not '= A'.
'1,2654' in the struck loghyp line: the true value is 1.26551.
